content.title: About
content.content: Fried oysters are a seafood dish made from fresh oysters that are coated in breadcrumbs or flour and deep‑fried until golden and crispy. They have a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy exterior while remaining juicy inside.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oysters can filter up to 50 liters of water per day, helping to clean their marine environment.
They have long been considered an aphrodisiac and are often served in romantic settings.
In ancient Roman cuisine, oysters were served with honey and vinegar.
Frying intensifies the aroma of oysters, though some nutrients may be lost in the process.
Oysters can grow up to 30 cm in span, but most market‑available ones are 5–10 cm long.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Oysters provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich source of zinc
items.content: A single serving of fried oysters supplies over 300 % of the daily zinc requirement, supporting immunity and skin health.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When lightly fried, oysters remain relatively low‑calorie with modest saturated fat content.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Oysters provide EPA and DHA, which are beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Oysters can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Improperly handled oysters may contain Vibrio bacteria, leading to foodborne illness.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Added salt during frying can raise sodium levels, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Heavy metals
items.content: Oysters can accumulate cadmium and lead; it is advisable to buy from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fried oysters hot as an appetizer, often with lemon wedges, tartar sauce, or a spicy dip. They can be added to salads, pasta, or rice dishes. For best texture, eat them shortly after cooking while the coating is still crisp.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fried oysters in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a sealed bag for up to 1 month, though the coating may lose some crispness after thawing.
